title: AI got me 80% of a character model. The last 20% required me to actually learn Blender.
author: thezirHaze
selftext:
Solo dev on LittleBigFoot, a cozy stealth adventure. I’ve posted here before about my AI asset pipeline, so this is the other half of that story.

My NPC base bodies came out of a generative tool and they were fine. Usable. Faceted hair with hard polygon edges, muddy topology around the face, but shippable if you squint. I kept trying to fix them by prompting and re-exporting and I kept getting different versions of the same problem.

So I dusted off Blender and did it by hand. Cleaned up vertices, fixed the topology around the head, separated the hair into its own mesh. Before and after in the images.

**The part that actually mattered had nothing to do with how the faces look.**

My main character’s vest had been modelled *into* his body as one mesh. That had been quietly causing problems for weeks and I’d been working around it rather than understanding it. Pulling it apart by hand is what made me realize clothing can’t be part of the body at all, it has to be separate geometry layered over a single body writer.

That realization is the entire reason I now have a disguise system. Ranger uniform, camper outfit, swappable from the equipment panel. I could not have properly designed that system before, because **I didn’t understand my own assets well enough to know what was possible.**

That’s the thing I’d pass on. AI will hand you an asset that works. It will not hand you a mental model of that asset, and you need the mental model to design systems around it. I spent several weeks treating my meshes as black boxes that arrived from a tool, and the cost wasn’t ugly models, it was a system I couldn’t see.

comments.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
comments.body:
Did AI do 100% of your reddit post too? What about the other 20%?

Seriously, I don't mind people discovering things like this, it's cool to see other people learn... But come on, don't disrespect everyone here with the lowest effort writeup of what you learned.

replies.author: thezirHaze
replies.body: As far as writing this, it was actually the other way around. I wrote 80% of it, and AI did the 20% by cleaning up my grammar lol

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body: My mistake then, I apologize.  Usually what gives it away is bold/italic text, bullet points, specific words fully spelled out or used at all "faceted" "muddy", starting sentences like "Cleaned up" etc. Nobody does those things.  I hope your project continues to go well.

replies.author: thezirHaze
replies.body: No worries! We are living in very interesting times (because AI and other things) lol

comments.author: space-bee-1
comments.body: Thank you for sharing! I’m also got stuck trying to work with outfits on models that ai generated. How long did it take you to learn what you did about blender?

replies.author: thezirHaze
replies.body: It took me a couple of minutes! Claude guided me through it step by step the first time. Did it on my own for the rest of the models.

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body: Stop wasting time on game assets! Go 100% procedural! 🔥
